_about: Named viewer settings (not to be confused with the repo root's capture_presets.json, which holds capture settings for the Python pipeline). Each key is a panel control's id and the value it is set to, exactly as if the slider had been moved by hand. 'reliefscale': 'grid' means match the grid size. Keys about the preset itself: 'short' is the button's text and 'label' its tooltip; 'view' presses a camera button; 'camera' frames a shot (azimuth and elevation in degrees, distance in tiles); 'research' shows the button only in Research mode; 'chapter' makes it a story step instead of a button, with 'caption' shown over the canvas ({tiles}, {size}, {world}, {scene}, {source}, {collects}, {exposed} are filled in from the tileset). Add your own; the viewer lists whatever is here.

plain.label: Just the capture: no terrain, no material rule, no far field. For scenes that are not ground tiles (garden, bicycle) and for comparing against the plain splats.

proof-on.label: rule on, for the on/off figure

proof-off.label: rule off, the same in every other way

ch1.label: One tile of ground, close up.
ch1.caption: 1 · capture One tile: {size} of {source}, rebuilt so that its four edges can meet other tiles. Everything that follows is built from {tiles} of these.

ch2.label: Wang tiles and their edge colours.
ch2.caption: 2 · tiles Wang tiles. Each edge carries a colour (the bands), and a tile may only sit next to one whose touching edge has the same colour, so any layout is seamless with no search. This part reimplements GSWT (Zeng, Ma and Sander, 2025).

ch3.label: The tiles laid over terrain, materials at random.
ch3.caption: 3 · world The same {tiles} tiles laid over generated, eroded terrain, {world} across, and the land carried on to the horizon. Here each tile's material is chosen at random: the baseline.

ch4.label: The same world with materials placed by the land.
ch4.caption: 4 · rule Now each material is placed by the shape of the land: {collects} collects in hollows and channels, {exposed} stays on steep and convex ground. This rule is the new part. Compare with step 3, or turn on "show the decision" under materials.
